correctness.rationale: The complete 35-facet presentation was reconstructed. A primitive annihilator of the 70 face-boundary relations and a 35-by-35 relation minor of determinant -1 prove that the first integral homology is infinite cyclic without relying on the published homology label. Exhaustive evaluation of all 120 graph triangles gives 70 faces, 40 primitive nonzero empty triangles, and 10 null empty triangles. Every claimed cyclic orbit and cone apex is enumerated by the standalone verifier. The proof is finite and exhaustive for this exact complex.

evidence: Altshuler 1977 classifies all 3677 neighborly ten-vertex combinatorial 3-manifolds and places the exact class in Class VI.
Kühnel--Lassmann 1985 gives the complete cyclic list through ten vertices and lists the exact type 2_10.
Köhler--Lutz 2005 reidentifies the object as a minimal vertex-transitive triangulation of the sphere product.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader classifications cover the object and its topological class but do not dominate the new statement: an abstract infinite-cyclic first homology group does not determine which of the fifty empty triangles vanish, their orbit multiplicities, or the existence and number of cone fillings.

value.rationale: The fifty empty triangles are the natural absolute first layer of simple cycles in a neighborly triangulation, so classifying their homology is a motivated combinatorial-systolic question rather than an arbitrary slice. The result adds a structural local-global statement: null-homology within that layer is detected exactly by a three-face cone filling, while all remaining forty cycles are primitive generators. The four essential cyclic orbits versus one null orbit gives a compact reusable description of the shortest homology shell.
